MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #12 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How many cents are in Ksh 5? (1 mark)
   A. 50 cents
   B. 500 cents
   C. 105 cents
   D. 5,000 cents

2. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 95, Ksh 140 and Ksh 260. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 395
   B. Ksh 505
   C. Ksh 495
   D. Ksh 595

3. One unit costs Ksh 15. What is the cost of 12 pencils? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 180
   B. Ksh 27
   C. Ksh 190
   D. Ksh 165

4. Kip faces North and makes a full turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. East
   C. South
   D. North

5. A tap is usually opened by turning it (1 mark)
   A. down
   B. anticlockwise
   C. up
   D. clockwise

6. Four quarter turns make (1 mark)
   A. a half turn
   B. a full turn
   C. a three-quarter turn
   D. a quarter turn

7. What do we call the point where the two arms of an angle meet? (1 mark)
   A. The arm
   B. The vertex
   C. The edge
   D. The side

8. At 3 o'clock the hands of a clock make (1 mark)
   A. a straight line
   B. a full turn
   C. a right angle
   D. a very small angle

9. How many corners does a cuboid have? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 6
   C. 4
   D. 8

10. Which fold gives a line of symmetry of a rectangle that is not a square? (1 mark)
   A. Along one of the short sides
   B. Across the middle from side to side
   C. Along a diagonal
   D. From one corner to the middle of the opposite long side

11. Which shape has three straight sides? (1 mark)
   A. Square
   B. Rectangle
   C. Circle
   D. Triangle

12. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with two equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 3
   C. 0
   D. 2

13. The table shows the favourite colours of 10 pupils: blue 4, red 4, green 2. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 12
   C. 11
   D. 9

14. In this grade we collect data of at most (1 mark)
   A. 5,000 items
   B. 10 items
   C. 1,000 items
   D. 100 items

15. In a tally chart, 4 more single tally marks are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 3
   C. 5
   D. 4

16. Why do we add up the totals in a table? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the data
   B. To change the data
   C. To make the table longer
   D. To check that the numbers are correct

17. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. car
   B. walking
   C. bus
   D. bicycle

18. The table shows the vehicles that passed a school gate (10 vehicles): matatu 5, boda boda 2, bus 2, lorry 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 9
   B. 11
   C. 10
   D. 12

19. The table shows the favourite colours of 10 pupils: blue 4, red 4, green 2. How many are NOT green? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 12
   C. 2
   D. 9

20. In a tally chart, one group of five and 1 more single tally mark are drawn. What number do they show? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 5
   C. 6
   D. 11

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write the steps for collecting and recording data about the favourite colours of 10 friends. (4 marks)

22. A group of five tallies and 3 more tally marks show which number? Explain how you count. (2 marks)

23. A gate opens through a half turn from its closed position. Describe the angle between the gate and the wall in its closed position. (2 marks)

24. Describe a pattern of shapes that you can make with squares and triangles, and write down the first six shapes. (3 marks)

25. Wanjiru buys 4 loaves of bread at Ksh 60 each, 2 packets of sugar at Ksh 155 each and 1 tin of cooking fat at Ksh 480. She pays with Ksh 2,000. (a) Find the total cost. (b) Find her change. (5 marks)

26. A learner writes 5 in the mango row but the tally shows 4. Explain why this is a mistake and how to avoid it. (3 marks)

27. A tally chart shows walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1 and car 1 for 10 pupils. How many pupils walk to school? How many do not walk? (3 marks)

28. Using the vehicle data (5 matatus, 2 boda bodas, 2 buses, 1 lorry), which type was seen most and how many more matatus than buses were seen? (3 marks)

29. List three properties of a square. (3 marks)

30. Draw a triangle and write down its number of sides and corners. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #12 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 500 cents
   Ksh 1 = 100 cents, so Ksh 5 = 5 × 100 = 500 cents.

2. C — Ksh 495
   Add the three costs: 95 + 140 + 260 = 495.

3. A — Ksh 180
   Cost = number × price = 12 × 15 = Ksh 180.

4. D — North
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a full turn gives North.

5. B — anticlockwise
   Most taps open when turned anticlockwise and close when turned clockwise.

6. B — a full turn
   Four quarters make one whole, so four quarter turns make one full turn.

7. B — The vertex
   The arms of an angle meet at a point called the vertex.

8. C — a right angle
   At 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand at 3, a quarter turn apart.

9. D — 8
   A cuboid such as a matchbox has 8 corners.

10. B — Across the middle from side to side
   Folding across the middle makes the two halves match exactly. A diagonal does not, because the corners do not fit on each other.

11. D — Triangle
   A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.

12. A — 1
   Only one fold, from the top corner to the middle of the base, makes the halves match.

13. A — 10
   Add all the numbers: 4 + 4 + 2 = 10.

14. B — 10 items
   To keep counting easy and accurate we collect at most 10 items.

15. D — 4
   0 × 5 + 4 = 4.

16. D — To check that the numbers are correct
   If the total does not match the number of items counted, we must count again.

17. B — walking
   The biggest number is 6, which belongs to walking.

18. C — 10
   Add all the numbers: 5 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 10.

19. A — 8
   10 − 2 = 8.

20. C — 6
   1 × 5 + 1 = 6.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide the question; ask each friend and make a tally mark; draw a table with a title and headings; write the totals and check they add up to 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8. Count the group of five as 5, then add 3 more: 5 + 3 = 8.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 8 and 1 mark for the explanation.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: They make a straight line, which is two right angles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a straight line and 1 mark for two right angles.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: square, triangle, square, triangle, square, triangle. The pattern repeats a square and a triangle in turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using both shapes, 1 mark for a clear repeating rule, 1 mark for six correct shapes.

25. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) Ksh 1,030 (b) Ksh 970
   Working / marking points: 4 × 60 = 240 (1 mark); 2 × 155 = 310 (1 mark); 240 + 310 + 480 = 1,030 (1 mark); 2,000 − 1,030 = 970 (2 marks).

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: The number in the table must match the tally, otherwise the total will not add up correctly. Count the tallies carefully and check the total.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mismatch, 1 mark for the effect on total, 1 mark for checking.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6 pupils walk. 10 − 6 = 4 pupils do not walk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 6, 1 mark for 10 − 6, 1 mark for 4.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Matatus. 5 − 2 = 3 more matatus than buses.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for matatu, 1 mark for 5 − 2, 1 mark for 3.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Four equal sides, four right angles and four lines of symmetry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct property.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of a triangle with 3 straight sides. It has 3 sides and 3 corners.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drawing and 1 mark for the numbers.
